statement: The exponential function e^x: the unique differentiable f with f' = f and f(0) = 1; equivalently sum x^n/n!, equivalently lim (1+x/n)^n; extended to C it gives Euler's formula.
essence: exp is the fixed point of differentiation: the one motion whose speed always equals its position. The number e, the series, compound interest and Euler's formula are all consequences of that single self-referential law 'rate = current amount'.
non_trivial_insight: The function comes first and the number is a byproduct. Every a^x is proportional to its own derivative, d/dx a^x = C(a) a^x; e is simply the unique base at which C(a) = 1. e is the output of a condition, not an input.

universal_offline_rules.gotcha: KaTeX refuses to render in quirks mode — the file MUST open with <!DOCTYPE html> and real <head>/<body>

katex.min.css resolves fonts by the relative path fonts/*.woff2, so the whole katex/ directory (css + js + fonts/) must be vendored intact — copying only the CSS silently falls back to system glyphs with no error

ESM-only builds cannot be loaded from file:// via a classic <script> tag (CORS origin: null) — every library must be vendored as a UMD/IIFE/global bundle from a CDN dist path, never from the GitHub source tree

CSS text-transform:uppercase on UI labels also re-cases KaTeX output (S_n -> S_N, e^x -> E^x, 1+x/n -> 1+X/N). Fix globally with `.katex, .katex * { text-transform: none !important }` plus an escape class for plain-text labels containing math

requestAnimationFrame is unreliable under headless Chrome's --virtual-time-budget, so animation-driven state cannot be verified with --dump-dom; drive the page over the DevTools protocol in real time, or seek the timeline manually
katex.min.css lists .woff2/.woff/.ttf per face; vendoring only .woff2 leaves two 404s per font offline (harmless online, visible offline). Strip the fallback src entries

library_specific: paper-core.min.js (not paper-full) is the right build for JS-driven use; paper-full bundles acorn for PaperScript (02)
Paper.js needs one PaperScope per canvas and scope.activate() before creating any item, because constructors insert into the ACTIVE project (02)
Paper.js items live in view coordinates — curves must be stored in world coords and re-projected on resize or everything drifts (02)
Path.simplify() on a nearly straight stroke legitimately returns a 2-segment path; guarding on segments.length < 3 silently kills the measurement — use arc length as the 'too short' test (02)
mathjs ships an ESM-only 'main'; the file:// path must point explicitly at lib/browser/math.js, which sets window.math (02)
math.simplify does not always reduce a genuinely-zero difference to '0' — drive verdicts from the NUMERIC residual and show the symbolic form only as corroboration (02)
mathjs returns Complex objects for e.g. sqrt(-1) rather than NaN, so sample loops must test isFinite() (02)
gsap .eventCallback('onComplete', fn) REPLACES an onComplete already set in the tween vars, silently dropping a commit step (03)
ECharts log axes reject zero values — map zeros to null and clamp the axis min to the smallest positive magnitude (03)
Object.assign(myOptions, DEFAULTS) puts defaults LAST and silently clobbers custom formatters — use Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, myOptions) (03)
Chart.js logarithmic axes draw a gridline at every minor tick, hatching the plot; a grid-color callback returning transparent for non-decade ticks fixes it, and tick labels need autoSkip:false (04)
a Chart.js canvas built inside a display:none tab panel initialises at zero size — call chart.resize() on first reveal (04)
p5.js instance mode is required to host two independent sketches without it hijacking the global namespace or auto-creating a stray canvas (04)
big.js multiplication is exact, so naive binary exponentiation doubles the digit count on every squaring — round to a fixed working precision after each multiply (04)
JavaScript bitwise operators coerce to int32, so `n & 1` silently corrupts exponents above 2^31 — use `n % 2` when n reaches 10^17 (04)
anime.js v3 defaults suspendWhenDocumentHidden = true and freezes every transition in a background tab — set it false at boot (05)
Three.js removed examples/js in r148, so r149 ships no globalised OrbitControls — vendor the r147 build, which is API-compatible (05)
Two.js makePath() calls center() on the path it creates, translating vertices out from under you — construct new Two.Path(...) + two.add() instead (05)
Two.js canvases are sized in logical units, so pointer coords must be rescaled by (logicalWidth / boundingRect.width) once CSS-scaled (05)
Three.js locked camera views need deliberate up-vectors; the naive (0,1,0) renders the sine wave upside-down (05)
design_and_correctness: a scroll fade-in that sets opacity:0 by default can leave the WHOLE page invisible if IntersectionObserver or the CSS transition misbehaves — apply the hidden state only after feature detection, with a timeout failsafe and prefers-reduced-motion opt-out (01)

gating section renders on a narrow centre-of-viewport band leaves sections holding stale values when a shared parameter changes off-screen — gate only expensive renders, on a generous root margin (01)

flagging table rows by 'error > tolerance' wrongly condemns rows that simply have not converged yet — measure against the legitimate truncation term instead, or the page implies the MATH is broken when only the ARITHMETIC is (01)
computing x^n/n! literally overflows to Infinity/Infinity = NaN for modest n — always use the recurrence (03)
absolutely-positioned animated elements need geometry recomputed on resize or they overlap on narrow viewports (03)
monospace tables with white-space:nowrap overflow narrow grid columns and clip silently; 1fr grid tracks let a wide table cause page-level horizontal scroll (03, 04)
KaTeX display math does not wrap — wrap every display block in overflow-x:auto and rebuild the widest with \begin{aligned} (05)
whitespace-only text nodes between inline-flex children are not rendered as flex items, gluing legend labels to adjacent KaTeX spans — use gap on the container (05)

a stray `*/` while editing a block comment kills an entire IIFE and the page renders as bare unstyled HTML with NO other symptom; --dump-dom alone reports nothing, only --enable-logging=stderr --v=1 surfaces it (04)
drawing 8760 risers plus a fill polygon every frame stalls the draw loop — stride the corner points once risers are sub-pixel (04)

math_honesty_flags_surfaced: 01: existence of C(a) = lim (a^h-1)/h is asserted, not proved; C(a) = ln a is revealed only AFTER e is hunted, so the reasoning is not circular; Math.E and Math.log appear exactly once each, both labelled as external checks

02: proves UNIQUENESS only — existence is explicitly deferred to 03; the Mean Value Theorem dependency ('derivative zero on an interval implies constant') is named at the step that uses it; every traced curve is labelled as RK4 with its measured deviation from the closed form

03: term-by-term differentiation of a power series is named as a licensed theorem (uniform convergence on compacts), not proved; uniqueness of power-series representation is stated as an assumption; direct summation of sum (-20)^n/n! is shown returning 173% relative error with no correct digits

04: the interchange of the limit in n with the infinite sum is asserted as provable, not proved; the negative-x staircase is shown ALTERNATING and giving $2.25 vs the true 0.0067; (1+1/n)^n in doubles is shown collapsing to exactly 1.0 at n = 10^16; every number carries an exact/70dp/64-bit provenance tag

05: e^{i theta} is DEFINED by the series (or by z'=iz), explicitly NOT 'e multiplied by itself i-theta times'; the split into cos and sin series is credited to absolute convergence (Riemann rearrangement named); forward Euler on z'=iz is shown spiralling outward as an instructive honest failure
cross-cutting: 04 explicitly contrasts its own slow e/(2n) convergence against 03's factorial 1/(N+1)! — 10 correct digits costs ~2.7e10 compoundings vs 13 series terms
corrections_during_the_run: The orchestrator's relayed brief for 04 quoted B_5(12) as 0.4774; the coder computed the stated product and found 0.381944, and used the correct value. The bracket product (1)(1-1/12)(1-2/12)(1-3/12)(1-4/12) = 0.381944.
